initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.thoughts:
**Reasoning:**  
The board is nearly empty with a single opponent 'x' at the bottom of column 3 (row 5, col 3). This is an early-game position where controlling the center (column 3) is critical in Connect 4, as it maximizes access to winning lines (horizontals, verticals, diagonals). Opponent has initiated in the center column, but only at the bottom. Playing in column 3 places 'o' at row 4, col 3, directly occupying the central high position, denying opponent a second piece there (which would give them a strong vertical stack in the center). Alternative moves (e.g., col 2 or 4) allow opponent to reinforce column 3 next (placing 'x' at row 4, col 3), gaining center control with two stacked pieces. No immediate threats exist, and column 3 offers the highest number of potential 3- and 4-in-a-rows (14 possible lines through center vs. fewer on edges). All columns are legal (row 0 empty everywhere). This move aligns with optimal Connect 4 opening strategy: contest the center immediately.

Final Answer: 3

The current board has all pieces stacked in column 3: opponent's 'x' at row 5 col 3, my 'o' at row 4 col 3, opponent's 'x' at row 3 col 3. No immediate threats exist for either player (no 2- or 3-in-a-rows to force blocks or wins). Column 3 has limited remaining space (next drop at row 2, only 4 rows used out of 6), making it suboptimal to continue stacking there, as it isolates my new 'o' (no adjacency to my existing 'o') and wastes vertical potential.

Optimal strategy: Drop in an empty adjacent column (2 or 4) at row 5 to create a connected diagonal two 'o's with the existing 'o' at (4,3):
- Column 2: 'o' at (5,2) adjacent diagonally to (4,3), forming a / diagonal two.
- Column 4: 'o' at (5,4) adjacent diagonally to (4,3), forming a \ diagonal two.

This maximizes early connectivity for future forks/threats (e.g., extendable to three at row 3 col 4 or row 3 col 2, respectively). The position is perfectly left-right symmetric due to vertical-only pieces in col 3, so columns 2 and 4 are equivalent in minimax value. Other columns (0,1,5,6) create isolated singles (worse heuristics/potential); col 3 creates an isolated second 'o' (worse).

In case of tie, select the lowest column index.
